layout: after connecting, the consumer sends the nonce as the first frame; every frame is u32 LE payload length + payload; payload at most 64 MiB, the nonce frame at most 256 bytes

streams.name: nonce-then-frames
streams.note: The first frame is the nonce; then frames flow, an empty payload is a frame, a panel stream frame is one payload.

streams.name: nonce-only
streams.note: The consumer sent the nonce and closed.

streams.name: frames-split-anywhere
streams.note: Framing is by length, not by write: the same bytes in any number of reads give the same frames.

streams.name: nothing-sent
streams.note: A consumer that closes before the nonce is refused.

streams.name: wrong-nonce
streams.note: A wrong nonce: the provider closes and reads nothing more; the channel is spent.

streams.name: nonce-prefix-only
streams.note: A nonce must match byte for byte, not as a prefix.

streams.name: nonce-with-extra-byte
streams.note: A nonce frame one byte longer is not the nonce.

streams.name: nonce-frame-too-long
streams.note: A first frame over 256 bytes ends the channel before anything is buffered.

streams.name: nonce-truncated
streams.note: A stream that stops inside the nonce frame is refused.

streams.name: frames-not-json
streams.note: A channel carries bytes; a JSON line is just a payload, never routed.

streams.name: truncated-length
streams.note: Stops inside a length prefix: the frames before it count.

streams.name: truncated-payload
streams.note: Stops inside a payload: the frames before it count.

streams.name: max-length-accepted
streams.note: A length of exactly 64 MiB is allowed (here the payload never comes).

streams.name: too-long
streams.note: A length over 64 MiB ends the channel; nothing of it is buffered.

streams.name: little-endian
streams.note: The length is little-endian: 01 00 00 00 is one byte.

ends.nonce: refused: no nonce, too long, or not the nonce; the provider closes
ends.truncated: closed inside a length prefix or payload
ends.too-long: a length prefix over 64 MiB; the reader closes the channel

pipes.note: What the SDKs make: pid, counter, module, channel.
Any name after the prefix of letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen.
Not a channel pipe (this is the router pipe's shape).
Another machine: never connected to (it would send the user's credentials).
Forward slashes are not the prefix.
The prefix is matched exactly, case included.
256 characters in all: the longest accepted.
